concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of facial crusted plaques, fever, and leukocytosis are consistent with Sweet syndrome, a condition characterized by acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis.
The patient's history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps, along with symptoms of bloody and watery diarrhea, are consistent with ulcerative colitis, a type of inflammatory bowel disease.
The patient's symptoms of painful subcutaneous nodules and septal panniculitis are consistent with erythema nodosum, a condition characterized by inflammation of the subcutaneous fat.
The patient's symptoms of facial crusted plaques and intradermal neutrophilic inflammation are consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum, a condition characterized by neutrophilic dermatosis.
The patient's history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps, along with symptoms of bloody and watery diarrhea, are consistent with Crohn's disease, a type of inflammatory bowel disease.
The patient's symptoms of polyarthralgia and skin lesions are consistent with psoriatic arthritis, an autoimmune disorder characterized by inflammation of the joints and skin.
The patient's symptoms of facial crusted plaques, fever, and leukocytosis are consistent with Behçet's disease, an autoimmune disorder characterized by inflammation of the blood vessels.

The patient's symptoms of polyarthralgia and inflammatory bowel disease are consistent with inflammatory bowel disease-associated arthritis, an autoimmune disorder characterized by inflammation of the joints.
